checks.name: Servers get credentialed scans
checks.description: Every in scope server was scanned with credentials, or by a local agent, within the scan window, so missing patches and local weaknesses are visible.
checks.remediation: Add scan credentials or install the scanner's agent on the listed servers.

controls.rationale: Shows servers were scanned in a way that can see missing patches. Patch deadlines and their tracking are checked in the vulnerability register.
Shows scans are deep enough to find local weaknesses. The policy and the remediation record stay with Verity's register and people.

Proposed successor control (server patching), only when adopted. Same rationale as EP-04: shows servers were scanned in a way that can see missing patches; deadlines and tracking stay with the register.

Proposed successor control (scanning coverage), only when adopted. Same rationale as LM-11: shows scans are deep enough to find local weaknesses; policy and remediation record stay with the register and people.

provider_notes.tenable: Asset attribute last_authenticated_scan_date [P45]. Least privilege user is Basic (16) with Can View on all assets.
provider_notes.rapid7: Asset field credential_assessments [P46]; its status values are unverified, so partial.
provider_notes.qualys: Host List Detection filters vm_auth_scan_date_after and vm_auth_scan_date_before [P48]. Reader user sees only the asset groups assigned to it.

checks.population: Assets in the scanner.scans_current population (Verity assets in service, status active or in_maintenance, of type infrastructure or cloud, in scope of the scanner connection, plus scanner assets matched to them) that run an operating system (scanner OS field present), excluding network devices the customer marks.
checks.predicate: The last authenticated scan, or the last agent scan, is within scan_window_days. Last agent scan field is unverified for every vendor.
checks.period: Rolling window of scan_window_days (default 30) back from the run.

parameters.scan_window_days: Default 30. Taken from the vulnerability management policy when it states one. Shared with scanner.scans_current.

checks.notes: Outcomes: pass; fail lists servers scanned only from the network; insufficient as for scanner.scans_current (assets with no scanner record while the customer has not confirmed the scanner account sees every asset; paging or export not finished); error on authentication, permission or API failure. The document says implementations stays empty until a collector ships; implementations here lists planned providers per the brief. NS-13 and LM-13 do not exist in objectives.json today (proposed successor codes). Framework reach (8.3): SOC 2 CC6.8, CC7.1; ISO 27001:2022 A.8.8. Not proposed (YAGNI, section 2.1): a separate SLA check per scanner (findings go into the register, judged once by verity.vulns.within_sla and verity.vulns.kev_owned); an external port scan check for NS-08 (a coverage need) is feasible from external scan findings but not proposed until a customer asks, NS-08 is served by cloud checks first. No observation type for scanner assets or findings exists in 01-evidence-model.md 1.4 (see defects).

checks.name: Application access list exports
checks.description: The complete list of members, guests and pending invites of a connected application account was read, with role and status, and dated.
checks.remediation: Connect the account with a role that can list every member.

controls.rationale: The access list a review starts from for this application. The review and its sign off are people's.
Lets leftover accounts in this application be found. Matching them to leavers is apps.members_active_in_directory.

provider_notes.grafana: Organisation users list needs an admin role (unverified); the minimal credential is a Viewer service account.
provider_notes.notion: Workspace members only; guests unverified. Users can be requested without emails by default; the connection sees only pages shared with it.
provider_notes.heroku: Team members; paths and fields unverified.
provider_notes.zendesk: Agents and admins; global OAuth required (D-P3-4).
provider_notes.posthog: GET /api/organizations/:organization_id/members/ (level, is_2fa_enabled, has_social_auth, last_login), scope organization_member:read.
provider_notes.sendgrid: GET /v3/teammates (user_type owner, admin or teammate; is_admin), scope teammates.read.
provider_notes.openai: GET /v1/organization/users and per project users and service accounts; Admin API key is read and write (D-P3-3).
provider_notes.anthropic: GET /v1/organizations/users, invites, workspace members; Console Admin API key allows writes (D-P3-3).
provider_notes.digitalocean: Team member listing not found in DigitalOcean's OpenAPI document (searched).

checks.population: All members, guests and pending invites of the connected account (workspace, organisation or team).
checks.predicate: The complete list was read, with role and status, dated.
checks.period: Point in time list, read weekly.
checks.empty_population: Not stated for this check; by the shared rules an empty list proves nothing and is insufficient_information unless the source shows the account really has no members.
checks.notes: Outcomes: pass when complete; insufficient when paging stopped or the provider shows only part (for example a token that sees one project); error. Tokens tied to one user may see only part of the account; every check treats not visible as insufficient and asks the customer to confirm full visibility once (section 9). ClickUp and Monday are not listed for this check. AI providers also implement it (section 2.3). Framework reach (8.3): SOC 2 CC6.2, CC6.3, CC9.2; ISO 27001:2022 A.5.11, A.5.16, A.5.18, A.8.4, A.8.30 (shared with apps.members_active_in_directory). Section 1.1 says this meets the operations research need for business_applications access lists.

checks.name: Application admins are named and approved
checks.description: Every member holding an owner or admin role in a connected application is a named, active person, approved in Verity with a review date not passed.
checks.remediation: Approve each listed admin in Verity, or remove the admin role.

controls.rationale: Lists who can administer this application and shows each was approved. Elevation and break glass use are not visible.

provider_notes.linear: Section 3.4 lists P (reason not given); section 8.1 omits it for Linear.
provider_notes.intercom: P, reason not given; admins list from Read admins scope.
provider_notes.anthropic: Roles admin, developer, billing, user, claude_code_user [P73].
provider_notes.digitalocean: Team member listing not found in the OpenAPI document.

checks.population: Members holding an owner or admin role (the document says the provider role map is in section 8; it is not, role fields are in sections 3 to 7).
checks.predicate: Every admin is a named person (not a shared mailbox), an active member, and marked approved on the connection by a person in Verity, with a review date not passed. Same per resource decision pattern as repository scope (AU-9).
checks.period: Point in time, read daily; approval must carry a review date not yet passed.
checks.empty_population: Not stated; by the shared rules an empty admin list is insufficient_information unless the source shows there really are no admins.
checks.notes: Outcomes: pass; fail lists admins not approved, shared or inactive; error; insufficient when roles cannot be read. Evidence kept: admins with role, last sign in where exposed, approval record. Needs a per admin approval record on the connection in Verity (UI and storage not described in the document). Section 8.2 says this meets the operations research need for admin role exports per tool (operations-checks.md section 6). Framework reach (8.3): SOC 2 CC6.3; ISO 27001:2022 A.8.2, A.8.18.

checks.name: Application requires company sign in
checks.description: A connected application account requires sign in through the company identity provider for every member, or each member allowed to bypass it has a recorded exception.
checks.remediation: Require single sign on for every member, or record an exception for each who must bypass it.

controls.rationale: Shows this application is inside single sign on. The list of all applications and approved exceptions stay with people.

provider_notes.grafana: Listed as unverified in section 3.1, not given a support level; left out of providers.
provider_notes.intercom: SSO status unverified (section 7.1); left out of providers.

checks.predicate: The account requires sign in through the company identity provider for every member, or lists the members allowed to bypass it and each has a recorded exception.
checks.period: Point in time setting, read daily.
checks.notes: Outcomes: pass; fail when not enforced; error; not_applicable when the provider has no SSO feature on the customer's plan (reason plan, shown once). Fills objective IAM-04.B of the artifact; exceptions (IAM-04.C) stay a person. Only one provider has any support today (Vercel, partial). The shipped idp.sso_enforced maps IAM-04 full; this one is partial. Framework reach (8.3): SOC 2 CC6.1; ISO 27001:2022 A.8.5.

checks.name: Application members use two factor
checks.description: A connected application enforces two factor, or every active member has it on, or sign in is single sign on only.
checks.remediation: Require two factor for the account, or ask the listed members to turn it on.

provider_notes.hubspot: Two factor field unverified; left out of providers.
provider_notes.intercom: Two factor status unverified; left out of providers.

checks.population: Active members of the connected account.
checks.predicate: The account enforces two factor, or every active member has two factor on, or sign in is SSO only (then the result says it relies on idp.mfa_enforced, and is insufficient when no identity provider is connected).
checks.empty_population: Not stated; by the shared rules an empty member list is insufficient_information.
checks.notes: Outcomes: pass; fail lists members without two factor; error; insufficient. Evidence kept: enforcement setting, per member two factor flag. Section 8.2 says this meets the operations research need for second factor per tool. Framework reach (8.3): SOC 2 CC6.1; ISO 27001:2022 A.8.5.

checks.name: Application members are current staff
checks.description: Each active member of a connected application matches an active identity provider user, or is recorded as an external or service member with an owner.
checks.remediation: Remove the listed members, or record each as an external or service member with an owner.

controls.rationale: Finds people who left but still hold this application, the outside single sign on case of IAM-12.D.
Finds contractor accounts that outlived their engagement in this application.

evidence_kinds: Member list compared with the directory

provider_notes.digitalocean: Team member listing not found in the OpenAPI document.

checks.predicate: Each member matches an active identity provider user (immutable id where the provider exposes one, else normalised email), or is recorded as an external or service member with an owner.

checks.empty_population: Not stated; by the shared rules an empty member list is insufficient_information.
checks.notes: Outcomes: pass; fail lists unmatched or disabled people; insufficient when no identity provider is connected or its list is incomplete; error. Evidence kept: member, match result, directory status. observation_types: the directory side is identity.user; the application side has no observation type in 01-evidence-model.md 1.4. checks.name: Application API keys are owned and in use
checks.description: Each active API key or token a connected application lists has a named owner and was used, or created, within the unused key window.
checks.remediation: Delete unused keys and give each remaining key an owner.

controls.rationale: Inventories machine credentials held in this application and finds unused ones. Rotation records for keys stored elsewhere stay with people.

provider_notes.resend: Reading needs a full access key (no read only key exists); recommended not to build (D-P3-3).
provider_notes.openai: Project api_keys and admin_api_keys expose created_at, last_used_at, expires_at, owner.
provider_notes.anthropic: GET /v1/organizations/api_keys has no last used field; creation age only.

checks.population: Active API keys and tokens the provider lists.
checks.predicate: Each has a name and an owner (person or service account), and was used, or created, within key_unused_days. Keys with full access where the provider offers a narrower type are listed.
checks.period: Rolling window of key_unused_days back from the run.
checks.empty_population: Not stated; by the shared rules an empty key list is insufficient_information unless the source shows no keys exist.

parameters.key_unused_days: Default 90. A key not used (or, without last use, not created) within this many days fails.

checks.notes: Outcomes: pass; fail lists ownerless or unused keys; insufficient when the provider does not expose last use (the check then judges creation age only and says so); error. The document is ambiguous here: it says both insufficient and judge creation age only when last use is missing; the merger should pick one (suggest: judge creation age and mark the result partial or insufficient, not pass). Whether full access keys fail or are only listed is not stated. Fills IAM-10.E of records-of-rotation-or-review (unused keys found). Section 2.3 says key hygiene is where most of the AI providers' real evidence is. Framework reach (8.3): SOC 2 CC6.1, CC6.3; ISO 27001:2022 A.5.16, A.8.3.

checks.name: AI data retention matches the review
checks.description: The data retention setting read from an AI provider equals the setting recorded on that vendor's engagement in Verity.
checks.remediation: Change the provider's retention setting, or update the vendor review to the setting in use.

controls.rationale: Shows the AI vendor's data handling still matches what the vendor review approved. The review and its report stay with people.
Shows prompts and outputs held by the AI vendor follow the retention set for that data. The schedule itself is a document.

provider_notes.openai: GET /v1/organization/data_retention and per project data_retention; type values zero_data_retention, modified_abuse_monitoring, enhanced_zero_data_retention, enhanced_modified_abuse_monitoring [P70].
provider_notes.anthropic: No retention endpoint in the Admin API reference (searched 2026-11-23); the document says the check is insufficient for Anthropic and the setting is contractual, so it stays a person's upload.

checks.population: The AI provider organisation, and each project or workspace with its own retention setting.
checks.predicate: The retention setting read from the provider equals the setting recorded on the vendor's engagement in Verity (for example zero data retention when customer data is sent).
checks.period: Point in time comparison, read daily.
checks.empty_population: Not stated; the organisation is always present, so the population is never empty when the connection works.
checks.notes: Outcomes: pass; fail names the difference; insufficient when the provider does not expose the setting (Anthropic today) or no expected value is recorded; error. Evidence kept: provider setting per scope, expected value, engagement. Assumes the Verity vendors module records an expected retention value on the engagement; the document does not say whether that field exists today. Fills DM-08.B and DM-08.D of data-retention-schedule (data held by the AI vendor) and the 'reviewed setting still holds' part of security-assessment-for-each-critical-vendor. Framework reach (8.3): SOC 2 CC9.2, P6.4, C1.2, P4.2; ISO 27001:2022 A.5.19 to A.5.23, A.8.10, A.5.33.

checks.name: AI usage is known and owned
checks.description: Every AI project, workspace and API key with recent usage is in scope on the connection with a recorded purpose and an owner who is an active member.
checks.remediation: Record a purpose and owner for the listed projects and keys, or disable them.

controls.rationale: Finds AI use nobody reviewed, the AI case of shadow IT. The decision to approve or remove it is a person's.
Each AI project carries a recorded purpose. Whether personal data is used for that purpose stays with people.

provider_notes.openai: Usage endpoints (GET /v1/organization/usage/completions and others) grouped by project and key; costs endpoint also available.
provider_notes.anthropic: Usage and cost analytics (beta) grouped by workspace_id and api_key_id; data from 1 January 2026, within the last 365 days, at most 31 days per request, typically within 4 hours and up to 24 hours [P74].

checks.population: Every project or workspace and every API key with usage in the last 30 days.
checks.predicate: Each is in scope on the connection with a recorded purpose (production, internal, trial) and an owner who is an active member; usage from anything unrecorded fails.
checks.empty_population: Not stated; no usage in 30 days would leave nothing to judge, which by the shared rules is insufficient_information rather than pass unless the provider confirms zero usage.
checks.notes: Outcomes: pass; fail lists unrecorded projects, workspaces or keys; insufficient when usage data has not landed (Anthropic data can take up to 24 hours); error. Evidence kept: usage per project and key, purpose, owner. Usage shows traffic, not content: whether personal data was sent stays with people. register-of-the-purposes-personal-information serves DM-07.B, DM-12.A, DM-12.B, DM-12.D, DM-12.E, DM-15.B in objectives.json; the document says 'DM-12.B and others'. Needs per project or key purpose and owner records on the connection in Verity. Framework reach (8.3): SOC 2 CC9.2, P4.1; ISO 27001:2022 A.5.23, A.5.34.

downgrades.reason: Implicit, per provider: the Controls touched rows for DigitalOcean, Supabase and Neon list NS-08 as partial, while the shipped mapping is full. The document does not propose changing the shipped mapping itself; the merger should decide whether coverage is stated per check or per provider.

Implicit: section 3.4 says IAM-01, where access requests are tracked in Linear or Asana, is partial for these ticketing tools. Shipped mapping is full.

decisions.question: Add capabilities business_applications and ai_providers, and add scanners (Tenable, Rapid7, Qualys) to asset_discovery?
decisions.recommendation: Yes; names match the coverage files.
decisions.source: connectors/phase3-catalogue.md Decisions for the owner D-P3-1, section 1.1

decisions.question: Fix the vulnerability module before any scanner ships: match assets on host identifiers, keep unmatched findings, carry first found time, explicit severity maps, scanner verified closure, provider external_id?
decisions.recommendation: Yes, fix first; without them a connected scanner makes the register look better than the estate.
decisions.source: connectors/phase3-catalogue.md Decisions for the owner D-P3-2, section 5.2

decisions.question: One ADR for providers whose API offers no read only credential (Render, Vercel, Netlify, ClickUp, Monday, Better Stack, Resend, OpenAI and Anthropic admin keys): accept with mitigations (dedicated lowest role user, expiring token, GET only allow list in the collector, shown to the customer), or do not build?
decisions.recommendation: Accept for OpenAI, Anthropic, Vercel; defer the rest; never build Resend.
decisions.source: connectors/phase3-catalogue.md Decisions for the owner D-P3-3, section 9

decisions.question: Register a Zendesk global OAuth client (Zendesk requires it for multi customer integrations; its Developer Terms forbid sharing API credentials with third parties)?
decisions.recommendation: Yes, before Zendesk is scheduled; lead time unknown.
decisions.source: connectors/phase3-catalogue.md Decisions for the owner D-P3-4, section 7.1

decisions.question: Notion: keep it in ticketing as partial, or treat it as a business application only?

decisions.recommendation: Business application only (access list); section 3.5 also recommends deferring Notion.
decisions.source: connectors/phase3-catalogue.md Decisions for the owner D-P3-5, sections 1.1, 3.5

defects.finding: notion is listed under ticketing but has no ticket model; a ticket check works only if the customer maps a database.
defects.proposal: Keep notion in ticketing only as partial, or move it to business_applications (D-P3-5; recommended business application only).

defects.finding: Vercel, Netlify, Render, Heroku and Qovery hold the deployment history the ci.* checks read, but ci_cd lists only github, gitlab and bitbucket.
defects.proposal: Add vercel, netlify, render, heroku, qovery to ci_cd.

defects.finding: qovery is listed under cloud_infrastructure, but section 4.8 gives its capabilities as ci_cd and business_applications only, because Qovery deploys onto the customer's own AWS, Google Cloud or Azure account and cloud checks come from that cloud's connector. Section 4.8 still lists cloud.environments_separated P for Qovery.
defects.proposal: Move qovery to ci_cd and business_applications; decide whether cloud.environments_separated stays implementable from Qovery's environment modes.

defects.finding: Vercel's firewall fits network_edge and implements edge.waf_enabled P, but vercel is not under network_edge.
defects.proposal: Add vercel to network_edge.

defects.finding: Section 1.1 says every SaaS in the file that exposes its members joins business_applications, including the platforms in section 4.
defects.proposal: Members: grafana, linear, asana, notion, digitalocean, heroku, render, vercel, netlify, supabase, neon, qovery, hubspot, intercom, zendesk, posthog, sendgrid, resend, openai, anthropic (see capabilities_proposed).

defects.finding: _ingest matches assets by asset_id or by name only (by_name = {r.name.lower(): ...}). Scanner hosts named by IP or FQDN do not match; they are counted as unmatched and dropped.
defects.proposal: Match on cloud_resource_id, fqdn, hostname, ip_address, primary_mac (all columns on assets), in that order; keep unmatched findings.

defects.finding: _ingest does 'unmatched += 1; continue', so a finding on an unregistered host disappears and the register looks cleaner than the estate.
defects.proposal: NEED verity_vulnerabilities: findings on hosts not in the asset register are kept as unmatched and raise asset register work (LM-01, proposed LM-13).

defects.finding: first_detected_at=now: the SLA starts when Verity first sees the finding, not when the scanner found it, so a first sync of an old backlog shows nothing overdue.
defects.proposal: NEED verity_vulnerabilities: imported findings keep the scanner's first found time and the SLA due date is computed from it (LM-11.D, LM-12.C). Requires a first_found field on FindingRow.

defects.finding: _SEVERITY_WORDS maps 0..4 and a few words; anything else becomes medium, so Rapid7 'severe' and Qualys level 5 would be stored as medium.
defects.proposal: Each collector maps its scale explicitly (section 5.3 maps: Tenable same words; Rapid7 none and informational to info, moderate to medium, severe to high, critical to critical; Qualys 5 critical, 4 high, 3 medium, 2 low, 1 info, QDS kept separately, to confirm with the KnowledgeBase). The module should reject an unknown severity instead of defaulting (code change for the module owner).

defects.finding: verify_instance closes only from pending_retest, by a person; a fix the scanner confirmed stays open until someone clicks.
defects.proposal: NEED verity_vulnerabilities: a finding the scanner reports fixed after a rescan moves to verified fixed with the scanner as verifier (actor System, the run's report), and every closure as fixed in the period has such a rescan or a person's retest (LM-11.E). The docstring already anticipates it.

defects.finding: _ingest does not set external_id per instance; a re-run cannot tell an instance from a new one by provider id, and the provider's own id is lost.
defects.proposal: Set source to the provider and external_id to the provider's finding or detection id (rule 9).

defects.finding: Coverage files raise a need against business_applications for this artifact ('business applications that hold personal data are listed'). The phase 3 research says these needs are met by the vendor register, not by the business application APIs.
defects.proposal: Point that need at the vendor register (verity_vendors) rather than business_applications.

defects.item: NEED cloud_infrastructure: preview and staging deployments require sign in
defects.finding: No check verifies that lower environments (preview and staging deployments) are not public (SD-12.C, DM-13.B). Raised for all section 4 platforms; Vercel exposes ssoProtection and passwordProtection on projects [P27], others unverified. Cloud research owns the cloud. prefix, so no key was proposed.
defects.proposal: Cloud research to propose a cloud.* key for this need.

defects.item: NEED (proposed SD-17): database audit logging on for every production database
defects.finding: Neon's settings.audit_log_level may meet this coverage need, but its meaning is unverified.
defects.proposal: Verify audit_log_level before mapping Neon to the SD-17 need.

defects.finding: Section 7.2 says SendGrid proves whether outbound TLS is enforced (NS-02 partial, for one channel; scope user.settings.enforced_tls.read) but names no check key for it.
defects.proposal: Merger to decide whether a check is needed; otherwise it stays person evidence.

defects.finding: Section 8.2 says 'The person source stays on each', but artifacts.json gives this artifact only a check source (verity.vulns.within_sla), no person source.
defects.proposal: Confirm whether a person source should be added (found by extraction cross check, not stated in the document).

defects.finding: Section 8.2 says the person source stays, but artifacts.json gives this artifact only a check source (verity.vendors.assessed_in_cadence).
defects.proposal: Confirm whether a person source should be added (extraction cross check).

defects.finding: Both are person only today. idp.mfa_enforced, vcs.org_two_factor_required and idp.sso_enforced feed no artifact at all, while the phase 3 document adds apps.mfa_enforced and apps.sso_enforced as sources.
defects.proposal: When the apps.* checks are added as sources, add idp.mfa_enforced and vcs.org_two_factor_required to the IAM-03 artifact and idp.sso_enforced to the IAM-04 artifact (extraction cross check; identity research may already raise it).
defects.source: artifacts.json cross check while verifying connectors/phase3-catalogue.md 8.2

defects.finding: Render, Vercel, Netlify, ClickUp, Monday, Better Stack, Resend, the OpenAI admin key and the Anthropic Console admin key cannot be made read only from what was found. integrations.md requires an ADR for a connector that needs write access.
defects.proposal: One ADR (D-P3-3) with mitigations: dedicated lowest role user, expiring token, GET only allow list in the collector, shown to the customer.

defects.finding: HubSpot logins 90 days, Render audit 90 days, Linear audit 90 days (Enterprise). A 12 month Type 2 period cannot be shown from the provider alone.
defects.proposal: Verity keeps its daily pulls as evidence (D-P3-6).

defects.finding: Qualys Readers and Tenable users without Can View on all assets, and app tokens tied to one user, see only part of the account.
defects.proposal: Every check treats not visible as insufficient and asks the customer to confirm full visibility once.

defects.finding: BMC Helix Discovery research is entirely unverified: the documentation site refused automated reading (HTTP 403), so REST API version, token flow, search endpoint and least privilege group are unknown. It is an enterprise tool, only for customers who already run it.
defects.proposal: Research again with documentation access or a customer's appliance before any build (D-P3-7).

defects.finding: integrations.md lists 'Tenable Nessus'; only Tenable Vulnerability Management was researched. Nessus API page not found, Security Center not read.
defects.proposal: Nessus Professional customers keep the existing .nessus upload path (parse_xml already reads ReportHost and ReportItem).

defects.finding: integrations.md lists 'Rapid7 Nexpose'; research covers InsightVM Cloud Integrations API v4 only; on premises Security Console API v3 not read. The v4 API also has Start Scan, Stop Scan and Update Scan Engine Configuration, so the user's role must not allow those. Read only role name and rate limits unverified.
defects.proposal: Use a user key of a read only user; research v3 before supporting on premises consoles.

defects.finding: Section 4.1 lists business_applications as a capability, yet team member listing and two factor status were not found in the OpenAPI document, so every apps.* check is N.
defects.proposal: Leave digitalocean out of business_applications until a member API is found.

defects.finding: Heroku warns that some read only resources can include write credentials in metadata.
defects.proposal: Collector keeps an allow list of fields; request scope read, not read-protected.

defects.finding: Audit logging may need to be switched on in the organisation's settings before events are kept (unverified).
defects.proposal: Until confirmed, an empty audit log is insufficient, never 'no admin actions'.

defects.finding: 01-evidence-model.md 1.4 defines no observation type for vulnerability_scanner (scanner asset, finding), business_applications (application member, API key, sign in setting) or ai_providers (retention setting, usage). The phase 3 document does not propose any.
defects.proposal: Add observation types for these capabilities before the checks are built (extraction observation).

defects.finding: Section 2.2 says the provider role map is in section 8; section 8 has no role map. Role fields are spread over sections 3 to 7 (Vercel owner, Supabase role_name, PostHog level, SendGrid user_type and is_admin, OpenAI owner, Anthropic admin roles; Heroku, HubSpot unverified).
defects.proposal: Write a role map per provider when the checks are built.

defects.finding: Not verified this round: BMC Helix Discovery entirely; SigNoz and Better Stack endpoints; ClickUp and Monday audit logs and scopes; Heroku, Render, Netlify and Qovery endpoint paths and fields; HubSpot scope names; Intercom and HubSpot two factor fields; Tenable export endpoint paths (names confirmed, paths not re read); Nessus Professional and Security Center APIs; Rapid7 read only role name and rate limits; Qualys severity names; OpenAI admin key creator and audit log activation; whether OpenAI's Go SDK covers admin endpoints; whether an Anthropic non admin key can read members and keys; whether a Grafana Viewer can read the alert provisioning API; Grafana's on call product; Grafana and Intercom SSO status.
defects.proposal: Verify each before the provider is built.

defects.finding: Vanta, Drata, Secureframe and Sprinto were not researched for any phase 3 provider; the shared web search budget was exhausted.
defects.proposal: Add per provider when its full connector document is written.

existing_check_changes.rationale: Make the definition precise so all three scanners mean the same thing. Population: Verity assets in service (status active or in_maintenance) of type infrastructure or cloud, in scope of the scanner connection, plus every scanner asset matched to them. Predicate: each asset has a scanner record whose last scan time is within scan_window_days (default 30, from the vulnerability management policy when it states one). Fail: assets whose last scan is older than the window. Insufficient: assets with no scanner record while the customer has not confirmed the scanner account sees every asset (Qualys Readers and Tenable users see only what they are granted); paging or export not finished. Error: authentication, permission or API failure. Empty population: insufficient_information. Frequency daily. Evidence kept per asset: Verity asset id, scanner asset id, last scan time, scanner name; unmatched scanner assets listed separately. Existing mappings LM-11 partial and EP-04 partial unchanged.

Add as a source of artifact actively-exploited-vulnerabilities-and-time-taken (LM-12.C), which is person only today, once the first found NEED (imported findings keep the scanner's first found time) is met. verity.vulns.kev_owned feeds no artifact in artifacts.json today. The check's shipped controls list only LM-11.
